about.what: Languages a translation may be published in.
about.contract: This list IS the upload contract. The website validates target_language against these names and the mod sends them, so a name added, removed or respelled on one side only shows up as an upload refused by a validation error the contributor did not cause and cannot read. It moves on every side at once or not at all.
about.identity: The NAME is the identity, never the tag. It is what the website stores, what the mod resolves to and what a game's config holds. Five of these have no ISO 639-1 code at all, which is a fact about a 1967 standard and not about a language.
about.tag: BCP 47. For most languages that is the familiar two-letter code, which is already a valid BCP 47 tag; the five without one carry the registered subtag instead - yue, prs, arz, ary, apc - each checked against the IANA Language Subtag Registry rather than written from memory. None of them is deprecated.
about.parent: Set only where the parent is itself an entry in this list, for grouping in a picker. Cantonese has none: its macrolanguage is zh, and this list has Simplified and Traditional Chinese, which are scripts rather than a language it is a variety of. Left empty rather than attached to something it does not belong to.
about.aliases: What somebody would actually type. Present only where a source gives one - the registry's own alternative descriptions here. Nothing invented.
about.providers: Absent on purpose. What Google Translate and DeepL accept is a fact about them, it changes without us, and it has to be taken from their own endpoints rather than typed from a documentation page. An empty or guessed field would read as knowledge.
about.not_the_website_interface: Unrelated to the 19 languages the website's own interface is translated into. Those are fixed and are a different question.
about.order: Same order as the website's config/languages.php, which is the reference for this list. Not because order carries meaning - it does not, the contract is checked by membership - but so that comparing the two sides is a diff anyone can read.
about.interface_fallback: When somebody's system asks for a language the website's interface does not have — Catalan, Breton, Basque — it serves ENGLISH. Uniformly, so no field carries it. The tempting alternative was to fall back to the majority language of the territory: Catalan to Spanish, Breton to French. It would often be more useful and it was rejected on purpose. It decides for somebody what else they speak, and routing a minority language to the language that displaced it is exactly the framing that makes those languages invisible elsewhere. English assumes nothing about anyone. ⚠ This is now a decision rather than an accident: the behaviour was already English, but only because an unmatched locale fell through to the default. Written down so it is not silently 'improved' later.
